fields.AN_Notes: Prompt experiment with ChatGPT (GPT-4) and Microsoft Copilot on four policy scenarios, each prompt variant submitted 50 times. General_Guidance: the work recommends 'precise, inclusive language in AI-assisted design and policy applications', i.e. explicitly naming the gendered target group in the prompt; it also states that inclusivity must not depend on prompting alone. Other_Task: drafting policy recommendations (policymaking, workplace and municipal policy design). Mitigation stages are recommendations in the conclusion: fine-tuning on curated gender-balanced and intersectional datasets (Pre_Processing, In_Training), equity principles in prompts (Prompt_Practice), audits, Human-in-the-Loop oversight and multidisciplinary teams (Organisational_Process); none is evaluated. Bias_Axes: only gender is varied; motherhood appears as a gendered role within the gender axis, race, class and ability are named only as intersecting factors in the discussion and are not analysed, so Intersectional is not coded. Social_Construct rests on the work's statement that gender relations are institutionally embedded in everyday practices; the work also uses biological metabolic differences as a factual premise. Erasure covers the omission of women's and non-binary needs in gender-unspecified prompts; Stereotyping covers baby-changing facilities placed only in women's restrooms.

fields.AN_Notes: Qualitative interpretative visual analysis of 180 Stable Diffusion XL images from minimal prompts, followed by a micro, meso and macro intersectional analysis. General_Guidance: users 'being more conscious of how they are generating images-e.g. what kind of prompts they use'; prompting otherwise serves as research instrument (deliberately minimal prompts to surface default outputs). Other_Task: image creation in creative and design practice. Bias_Axes: Language_Culture codes the Global North and US-centric cultural representations (food, settings), Nationality_Migration the immigrant/citizen prompts, Socioeconomic poverty/wealth and blue/white collar, Physical_Appearance the absence of larger or smaller bodies, Sexual_Orientation_Identity the heteronormativity and absence of non-binary representation the work reports; religion was explicitly excluded by the authors. Mitigation proposals: better curation of training data (Pre_Processing), conscious prompting by users (Prompt_Practice), regulation, criminal culpability, diverse teams and algorithmic reparation (Organisational_Process); none evaluated. Bias_Definition Implicit_Only: bias is framed through power systems and intersectionality without a sentence defining bias or discrimination. Toxicity was considered for the confederate flag imagery and left uncoded, since the work describes a violent symbol rather than language attacking a group.

fields.AN_Notes: Soft prompt tuning: a few trainable prompt embeddings are concatenated to the input of frozen encoder-only models (BERT, RoBERTa) and trained with a KL-divergence loss on gendered templates; evaluated on SEAT, StereoSet and pseudo-perplexity against CDA, Dropout, INLP, SentenceDebias and Self-Debias, with debiasing on par with the state of the art and limited loss of language modelling ability. Generative_KI is teilweise because the models are encoder-only masked language models, not generative systems. AN_Prompt_Techniques None: learned soft prompts fall under no technique family; in-context learning is cited only as motivation. Mitigation stage In_Training for the trained prompt parameters and Prompt_Practice for the change of model input; Evaluated. Race_Ethnicity and Religion are measured as side effects on StereoSet race and religion tests. Bias definition Explicit through the technical StereoSet criterion. Harm types named from Gallegos et al. in the introduction are cited, not coded; only Stereotyping is measured. AN_Task None: benchmark study without an application task.

fields.AN_Notes: Audit study with 42 prompt templates in five scenarios (purchase, chess, public office, sports, hiring), names perceived as Black or white and male or female, three context levels, six LLMs. General_Guidance: 'providing the model with a numeric anchor' (decision-relevant numeric context in the prompt) reduces name-based disparities, while qualitative context has inconsistent effects; this prompt practice is evaluated in the work's own experiment (Evaluated), routine audits at deployment are recommended (Organisational_Process, Proposed). Other_Task: advice for laypeople on purchase negotiation, salary offers in hiring, election and sports predictions. Intersectional is coded because Black female-perceived names receive the worst outcomes compared with Black and with female names; the authors themselves state that this analysis does not equate to an evaluation of intersectionality. Indirect_Discrimination follows the codebook anchor (name as proxy, disparate impact); the work's attribution of the disparities to encoded stereotypes is treated as explanation of the mechanism, not as a separate Stereotyping harm. Theory reference: the U.S. legal doctrine of disparate treatment and disparate impact frames the notion of bias.
